author: TEDx Talks
description:
Chronic conditions are something that effects a large portion of the population. Despite this, workplaces are not designed to support individuals with chronic conditions. It is important to reimagine the workplace and identify specific strategies employers can use to support employees with chronic conditions better.

Alyssa McGonagle is an Associate Professor of Psychological and Organizational Science at the University of North Carolina at Charlotte. Alyssa has been studying the challenges that workers and organizations face around chronic health conditions, and how to address them, for the last 15 years. Alyssa recently published a book on the topic titled, “Chronic Health Conditions and Work: Proactive Strategies for Supporting Employees and Doing Well by Doing Good." 

This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Why do people hide chronic illness at work? | Alyssa McGonagle | TEDxUNCCharlotte

author: TEDx Talks
description:
At seventeen years old, top of her class, prom queen, and dreaming of the Ivy League — Tsion Michael walked into her guidance counselor's office and was told five words that were supposed to end her story:

"Your future is illegal."

What followed was a decade in the shadows. No college financial aid. No legal path forward. No certainty about tomorrow. Tsion was undocumented — not because her family had done anything wrong, but because her father, a multilingual CPA and strategic leader, made the courageous choice to go all in for the liberation of his people in Eritrea. That sacrifice triggered a legal consequence none of them saw coming.

In this riveting, deeply personal TEDx talk, Tsion introduces the concept of the Rented Identity — the suffocating experience of performing a restricted version of yourself that does not technically belong to you.  She traces her decade-long fight from the shadows to citizenship. And she reveals the unexpected truth she found on the other side: the
title: From Undocumented to Unprecedented | Tsion Michael | TEDxThird Ward Salon

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What happens if you're never chosen?

From an early age, many women are taught that life begins after someone chooses them, a partner, an employer, an opportunity. We learn to wait for permission, validation, and the "right time" before building the lives we truly want.

In this TEDx talk, Krysta Monet explores what happens if that moment never comes and why waiting to be chosen may be one of the greatest limitations we place on ourselves. 

Through her deeply personal decision to become a single mother by choice, she challenges the belief that a meaningful life must follow a traditional timeline and offers a new perspective on agency, courage, and creating a life on your own terms.

This isn't a talk about motherhood. It's about identity, possibility, and the quiet revolution that begins when we stop asking, "Who will choose me?" and start asking, "What will I choose for myself?" Krysta Monet is a writer, speaker, and cultural commentator exploring the complexities of modern womanhoo
title: Single Mother by Choice | Krysta Monet | TEDxThird Ward Salon

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What do the world’s greatest innovators, entrepreneurs, and everyday problem-solvers have in common? They all faced moments where they had no idea what to do next.

In this inspiring and practical TEDx talk, David Settle introduces the concept of “Figure-It-Out-ness”—the often-overlooked skill of navigating uncertainty with curiosity, resilience, and action. Drawing from his experiences as an entrepreneur, educator, celebrity photographer, and tech startup founder, David challenges the belief that success comes from always having the right answers. Instead, he reveals how embracing the words “I don’t know” can become the catalyst for innovation, growth, and breakthrough.

Blending personal stories, humor, and actionable insights, this talk equips audiences with a framework for tackling life’s biggest challenges when the path forward isn’t obvious. Whether you’re building a business, leading a team, pursuing a dream, or simply facing an uncertain future, you’ll leave with the confidenc
title: Figure-It-Out-ness: What to Do When You Don’t Know What to Do | David Settle | TEDxThird Ward Salon

author: TEDx Talks
description:
In "No Such Thing as 'Fast'," Alexus Grace (Rhone) examines how flawed social science research became cultural shorthand that mischaracterized Black girls as “fast” and families as “broken.” Tracing these labels from academic studies to everyday language, she reveals how data without context can harden into identity—shaping not only perception, but lived experience.

Blending personal narrative, cultural analysis, and storytelling practice, Alexus introduces “re-storying” as a corrective approach—one that restores complexity, dignity, and agency to lives flattened by oversimplified conclusions. She challenges the assumption that research is neutral, reframing it instead as a powerful narrative force that must be handled with care.

Ultimately, this talk expands beyond one community to ask a universal question: What happens when people are defined before they are fully formed? In an era where more people than ever have the tools to shape stories, Alexus invites us to take responsibilit
title: No Such Thing as 'Fast' | Alexus Grace Rhone | TEDxThird Ward Salon

author: TEDx Talks
description:
For years, we've lived in an attention economy where followers, likes, and virality determined who was seen, trusted, and rewarded. But artificial intelligence is quietly changing the rules.

In this thought-provoking talk, physician-turned-entrepreneur Dr. Christopher H. Loo, MD-PhD argues that we're entering an era where authority—not attention—will become the most valuable currency. As AI-powered search and answer engines increasingly determine what information people discover and trust, long-term credibility, evidence, and a body of work matter more than ever.

Drawing from his own journey of leaving medicine during the 2008 financial crisis, rebuilding his career through media and technology, and hosting more than 1,500 podcast conversations, Dr. Loo reveals why the future belongs to those who build trust instead of chasing trends.

If AI is rewriting the rules of influence, trust, and opportunity, what should we be building instead? Dr. Christopher H. Loo, MD-PhD, is a physician
title: Why AI Will End the Attention Economy | Christopher Loo | TEDxThird Ward Salon

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if the most important map you’ll ever explore isn’t the world—but yourself?

In this thought-provoking talk, Dr. Gail Awan introduces J.O.G.I.™ (Journey • Origin • Geography • Identity), a framework that explores how history, ancestry, geography, and personal experience shape the stories we tell about ourselves and others. Drawing from science, history, culture, and storytelling, she challenges audiences to see identity as something richer than labels or DNA alone.

Through an unexpected conversation with Wilma Flintstone, Dr. Awan invites us to ask a timeless question: What kind of ancestor will you become? The result is a fresh perspective on empathy, belonging, and the legacy each of us has the power to create. Dr. Gail Awan is a nonprofit executive, cultural storyteller, author, and two-time TEDx speaker with more than 25 years of experience leading community-based initiatives. She is the creator of J.O.G.I.™ (Journey • Origin • Geography • Identity), a storytelling framework
title: Coffee with Wilma Flintstone | Gail Awan PhD | TEDxThird Ward Salon

author: TEDx Talks
description:
The reality of the AI revolution, and an optimistic guide to navigating uncertainty and constant change.

 Professor Michael Milford is a globally recognised researcher, the Director of the QUT Centre for Robotics, and one of Australia’s leading voices on the opportunities and risks of AI and robotics. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: What experts aren't telling you about AI | Prof. Michael Milford | TEDxQUT

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if your greatest strength isn't something you built but something you survived? In this talk, Elena Sarango-Muniz challenges the way we think about professional excellence. After 25 years in HR, she discovered that the qualities making leaders exceptional often trace back to childhood wounds... to old verdicts we've spent our careers trying to overturn. Your perfectionism, your caretaking, your relentless drive, they all have a story. But here's the paradox: stitched wounds are not the same as healed wounds. Learning to live with what shaped us isn't weakness. It's wisdom.
 
This talk is for anyone who's ever wondered why they work so hard, who they're really trying to prove something to, and what might change if they stopped trying to erase their wounds and started learning from them instead. Elena Sarango-Muniz is an executive coach and former HR leader with 25 years in global corporate environments. She works with senior leaders to uncover how their greatest professional stren
title: Stitched is not healed | Elena Sarango-Muniz | TEDxThird Ward Salon

author: TEDx Talks
description: Equip children with the resilience and emotional intelligence required to navigate challenges, bounce back from setbacks, and thrive. Kari is an accomplished author, educator and researcher with more than 30 years’ experience in education, wellbeing and human development. Author of 'Raising a Mentally Fit Generation', Kari is passionate about translating emerging science into practical, evidence-informed strategies that help schools and families support young people to thrive. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Fences, not ambulances! | Kari Sutton | TEDxQUT

author: TEDx Talks
description:
For generations, we've celebrated the loudest voices as the strongest leaders. We've been taught that confidence looks like speaking first, speaking often, and commanding every room we enter.

But what if we've been measuring influence all wrong?

In this talk, Michelle Gines introduces the concept of the Quiet Extrovert, someone who is energized by people yet leads through observation, intentionality, and meaningful connection rather than constant visibility. Drawing from her own experiences in leadership, publishing, and personal transformation, she shares how quiet influence often creates deeper trust, stronger relationships, and more sustainable impact than attention alone.

Using her M.O.R.E. Framework, Michelle offers a practical approach for recognizing and embracing a leadership style that has too often been overlooked. Rather than encouraging people to become someone they're not, she invites them to become more fully themselves.

This talk challenges the belief that influence
title: The Quite Extrovert Advantage: Say Less, Become M.O.R.E. | Michelle Gines | TEDxThird Ward Salon

author: TEDx Talks
description: O que guardamos nos porões que existem dentro de nós? Sônia Bossolani usa essa metáfora para falar sobre lembranças dolorosas, ressentimentos e sentimentos que tentamos esconder, mas que continuam influenciando nossa vida. Ao compartilhar a perda de uma sobrinha em um acidente e o longo processo de elaborar o luto, ela revela como encontrou, atrás da dor, uma culpa que ainda precisava ser compreendida. Um relato íntimo sobre a coragem de iluminar nossas feridas, rever julgamentos e reconhecer a humanidade em nós e nos outros — abrindo espaço para o perdão, a libertação e a paz. Sônia Bossolani é gestora social e atua há décadas no desenvolvimento de projetos voltados ao acolhimento e à proteção de crianças, adolescentes e famílias em situação de vulnerabilidade. Ao longo de sua trajetória, construiu uma carreira marcada pelo compromisso com o cuidado, a escuta e a promoção da dignidade humana. Sua experiência profissional a colocou em contato com histórias de superação, resiliência e
title: O porão | Sônia Bossolani | TEDxAraraquara

author: TEDx Talks
description: O que significa ser visto de verdade? Patrícia Assunção relembra momentos em que se sentiu invisível — na infância, na adolescência, no casamento e até trabalhando em seu próprio bar — para refletir sobre quantas pessoas atravessam a vida sem serem verdadeiramente notadas. Ao reencontrar o teatro e desenvolver oficinas com mulheres em situação de vulnerabilidade, ela descobre que recuperar a voz é também recuperar presença, dignidade e existência. Por meio de encontros capazes de reconstruir vínculos e transformar histórias, Patrícia nos convida a abandonar a indiferença e fazer algo simples, mas profundamente humano: olhar, enxergar e reparar. Patrícia Assunção é atriz, educadora e produtora cultural que acredita na arte como ferramenta de encontro, pertencimento e transformação social. Ao longo de sua trajetória, desenvolveu projetos que utilizam o teatro para ampliar vozes frequentemente ignoradas e criar espaços de expressão para pessoas em situação de vulnerabilidade. Seu trabalh
title: A arte traz à luz as humanidades que aprendemos a ignorar | Patrícia Assunção | TEDxAraraquara

author: TEDx Talks
description: O que perdemos quando deixamos de cozinhar e passamos apenas a consumir? A partir das memórias de uma infância cercada por hortas, receitas de família e encontros ao redor do fogão, Katleen Lacerda reflete sobre como a pressa, a publicidade e os alimentos ultraprocessados estão transformando nossa relação com a comida. Unindo gastronomia, cultura e experiência pessoal, ela defende que comer bem é mais do que nutrir o corpo: é preservar histórias, fortalecer comunidades e exercer um direito. Um convite para recuperarmos a consciência sobre o que colocamos no prato e reconhecermos a cozinha como espaço de afeto, sustentabilidade e resistência. Katleen Lacerda é chef de cozinha, empreendedora e pesquisadora dos sabores que atravessam gerações. Inspirada pelas memórias construídas ao redor da mesa, transformou a herança culinária de sua família em uma trajetória marcada pela valorização da cultura, da identidade e das histórias que vivem na comida. Seu trabalho une técnica, criatividade e
title: Conhecendo e reconhecendo sabores | Katleen Lacerda | TEDxAraraquara

author: TEDx Talks
description: Como preparar a sociedade para decisões capazes de afetar o clima do planeta? Partindo dos riscos associados aos eventos climáticos extremos, o comunicador Ronesier Corrêa apresenta o debate sobre tecnologias de modificação climática e defende que ele não permaneça restrito aos círculos científicos. Ao relembrar sua trajetória na comunicação e investigar experiências históricas de produção de chuva atribuídas ao cientista Frederico de Marco, ele encontra em Araraquara um ponto de conexão entre ciência, memória local e participação cidadã. Uma reflexão sobre a importância de tornar temas complexos acessíveis, estimular o pensamento crítico e envolver a sociedade nas escolhas que podem moldar o nosso futuro climático. Ronesier Corrêa é jornalista investigativo, produtor de arte e pesquisador dedicado ao resgate de histórias que o tempo quase deixou para trás. Ao longo de sua trajetória, tem atuado na preservação e divulgação da obra de personagens fundamentais da ciência brasileira, com
title: Do passado ao futuro: Araraquara e o debate sobre geoengenharia | Ronesier Corrêa | TEDxAraraquara

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Is Our Early Intervention System Failing Children Who Need Support Most? is a compelling TED Talk by Dr. Essence Presley that challenges the way society responds to young children with developmental delays. Drawing from decades of experience in early childhood and special education, Dr. Presley exposes the growing gap between children who qualify for early intervention services and the limited workforce available to serve them. She argues that children are not simply "falling through the cracks"—they are being left behind by a system that cannot keep pace with increasing demand during the most critical years of brain development.

Rather than focusing solely on the problem, Dr. Presley presents an innovative, workforce-based solution that expands the circle of support beyond licensed specialists. She advocates for equipping parents, childcare providers, educators, and community members with foundational skills to recognize developmental delays and provide meaningful early support. Thr
title: A new approach to early intervention for children | Essence Presley | TEDxThird Ward Salon

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if belonging is not something we wait to receive, but something we choose to create?  
In this powerful TEDx talk, Khady Gaye introduces the world to Teranga—a Senegalese concept that goes far beyond kindness. Teranga Is a way of leading, living, and connecting that transforms strangers into community and workplaces into spaces where people feel seen, valued, heard, and respected.

Drawing from her personal journey across continents, cultures, and boardrooms, Khady challenges us to rethink what it truly means to welcome others. She shows that belonging is not a soft skill—it’s a human and leadership imperative for all of us, whether we’re managing teams, coordinating non‑profit programs, hosting community networks, or bringing people together at home

This talk is an invitation to lead differently, connect more deeply, and discover how one simple act of genuine welcome can change lives, teams, and communities. Born and raised in Ghent with Senegalese roots, Khady Gaye is a multil
title: Teranga: Why belonging begins with welcome | Khady Gaye | TEDxThird Ward Salon

author: TEDx Talks
description:
How can one little girl who cannot speak change the way we think about healthcare, education, government, leadership—and even artificial intelligence?

After becoming the primary carer for her daughter with profound disabilities, Christine Stow discovered that the greatest barriers to progress are often not a lack of resources, but the assumptions hidden inside the systems we create. Through deeply personal stories and powerful real-world examples, she explores why lasting change begins by questioning the way we think—not simply building bigger systems. In an era where AI will increasingly shape our institutions, this talk is a timely reminder that technology can only amplify the quality of the thinking behind it. Christine Stow is a TEDx speaker and strategic thinker who helps people and organisations change the way they see so they can change what's possible.

Drawing on her experience as a corporate executive, elected local government leader, and primary carer for her daughter with
title: What caring for my daughter taught me about broken systems | Christine Stow | TEDxThird Ward Salon

author: TEDx Talks
description: For generations, many Christians inherited a familiar story: stay faithful, serve God, and eventually marriage will come. But what happens when the world changes while the advice stays the same? Through humor, research, and cultural observation, Sekou Browne explores how demographic shifts have quietly transformed Christian dating—and why many faithful people aren’t failing as much as they’re navigating a different world than the one the advice was written for. Sekou Browne is a writer, filmmaker, and cultural commentator exploring the intersection of faith, relationships, and modern culture. Across essays, fiction, film, and public conversations, his work examines the stories people inherit—and what happens when those stories no longer match the world they live in. He is the founder of Yoked, a publication examining modern Christian singleness, and the author of the forthcoming novel Coming Up Short. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independentl
title: Your pastor can’t find you a husband | Sekou Browne | TEDxThird Ward Salon

author: TEDx Talks
description: We go on a Gambling Journey - the current state of gambling, what happens in our brains and how to stay stopped from gambling. Speaker, Podcaster and Coach, Hugo helps Gamblers, Alcoholics and Addicts find Recovery. Over 25+ years in the arena allows Hugo the perspective from the suffering person to being recovered. Changing how Recovery works. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: The dark world of gambling | Hugo Vrsalovic | TEDxThird Ward Salon

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Minority adoption in the USA now Lemar Marie Brown is a corporate board director and retired a career with Shell plc and Goldman Sachs. She is a former Executive Professor at the Mays Business School at Texas A&M University, where she continues to guest lecture. Lemar earned an MBA in Finance from The Wharton School of the University of Pennsylvania and a Bachelor of Science in Mechanical Engineering from Northwestern University.

Most audiences know Lemar for her expertise in win-win negotiations. This TEDx Talk, however, reflects a deeply personal mission.

Her first board was with CASA (Court Appointed Special Advocates), advocating for children navigating the foster care system. Through that experience, she learned that African American children are disproportionately represented in foster care and are adopted at lower rates than children of other racial backgrounds. When she and her husband decided to start a family, that knowledge led them to pursue adoption.

In this TEDx Talk,
title: The joy of brown eyes | Lemar Brown | TEDxThird Ward Salon

author: TEDx Talks
description: It's nearly midnight. The house is quiet. And you're opening the laptop again, because that's what leadership requires. Right? In this talk, CEO Davide Viola dismantles the leadership playbook we all inherited, work harder, stay later, carry more, and shows how it quietly damages our health, our homes, and our companies. Drawing on his MBA research into why businesses fail, a fintech CEO's stage 4 cancer wake up call, and his own company's rise from an employee NPS of 38 to a world class 80, he makes the case that leadership as we've defined it is incomplete. The tools to serve both people and profit are here now. Because we only get one life to lead, and it doesn't happen by default. It happens by design. Davide Viola is the President and CEO of Health First Network, a national organization supporting 160+ health and wellness retailers across Canada. Fortune 500 trained, he has spent 25+ years leading in CPG, retail, and healthcare across Canada and the U.S., including leadership of
title: Why the best leaders design for people, not just profit | Davide Viola | TEDxThird Ward Salon

author: TEDx Talks
description:
In un mondo in cui l'intelligenza artificiale è sempre più capace di imitare il nostro lavoro, cosa significa davvero essere presenti?
Jacopo Romei esplora il confine tra accesso e presenza, mostrando come la vera differenza non stia nella qualità tecnica di ciò che produciamo, ma nella responsabilità, nell'intenzione e nelle relazioni che siamo capaci di costruire.
Perché la presenza autentica non può essere automatizzata: resta il tratto più umano e il valore più difficile da replicare. Ha scritto il primo codice nel 1984 su un Commodore 64 e ha iniziato a programmare per lavoro nel 1996. Entro il 2011, aveva già fondato tre aziende e ne aveva chiuso due. Ha introdotto i metodi agili in eBay, Siemens, FAO e molte altre corporation. Ha sempre creduto che parlare in pubblico fosse un'attività cruciale per diffondere il suo messaggio, validarlo e promuoverlo. 
Oggi Jacopo aiuta aziende, startup e professionisti a costruire nuove imprese, minimizzando il loro rischio e massimizzando il
title: Il confine tra accesso e presenza | Jacopo Romei | TEDxMessina

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Chiara Borgia affronta uno dei confini più delicati dell'essere adulti: quello tra il desiderio di proteggere i bambini e la necessità di dire loro la verità.
Attraverso esempi concreti, il contributo della neuropedagogia e della Death Education, mostra come il silenzio e le bugie non proteggono davvero i più piccoli, ma li privano degli strumenti per dare senso alle proprie emozioni.
Il suo talk è un invito ad abitare l'incertezza insieme ai bambini, restando accanto a loro con ascolto, autenticità e fiducia nelle loro risorse. Si occupa di sostegno alla genitorialità, accompagnando genitori, bambine e bambini nei passaggi delicati della crescita.
È specializzata in Neuropedagogia e Death Education ed è operatrice Touchpoints Brazelton. Direttrice responsabile di Uppa e autrice di testi divulgativi dedicati all’infanzia e all’educazione. Svolge attività di formazione con professionisti di ambiti diversi, promuovendo uno sguardo integrato e transdisciplinare nel lavoro educativo e di
title: Quando i bambini restano soli | Chiara Borgia | TEDxMessina

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Patients often believe withholding information protects them from judgment, embarrassment, or difficult conversations. In reality, those omissions can have life-threatening consequences.

In this compelling TEDx Talk, Dr. Shiela R. Ford, a nurse, educator, and healthcare leader with more than 32 years of experience, explores why patients sometimes choose not to tell the truth and how fear, shame, mistrust, and communication barriers can compromise clinical decision-making. Through powerful personal stories and real-world healthcare experiences, she challenges audiences to rethink the role of trust in patient care.

Dr. Ford argues that trust is not a soft skill but a clinical necessity. When patients feel psychologically safe enough to be honest, healthcare providers can make better-informed decisions, improve outcomes, and strengthen the relationships at the heart of quality care.

This talk is a call to action for patients, healthcare professionals, educators, and healthcare organiz
title: Why do some patients lie? | Shiela Ford | TEDxThird Ward Salon

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Antonello Sidoti parte da una domanda semplice: e se il confine più difficile da superare fosse proprio il nostro Io?
Attraverso la sua esperienza nella scuola di italiano per migranti Penny Wirton racconta come l'incontro con l'altro riesca a scardinare paure, pregiudizi e indifferenza. Le storie di ragazzi, famiglie e rifugiati mostrano che ogni relazione autentica è capace di trasformare non solo chi arriva, ma anche chi accoglie.
Il suo è un invito a riconoscere i diritti fondamentali di ogni persona e a lasciare che l'Io si apra fino a diventare un "noi". Da 41 anni si occupa di dipendenze e disagio giovanile. Musicista e referente provinciale del programma “Nati per la Musica”. 
Nel 2013 fonda l'associazione “Wind of Change”, la cui sede operativa è una biblioteca di quartiere, dentro la quale opera la scuola di italiano per stranieri “Penny Wirton”. 
Collabora con i dipartimenti Scipog e Cospecs dell'Università di Messina in qualità di Tutor per i tirocini formativi del CdS in
title: Io come confine del "Noi" | Antonello Sidoti | TEDxMessina

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Have you ever built a life that looked absolutely perfect from the outside, only to realize it wasn’t actually yours?

In this moving and witty talk, business owner and US Marine veteran Bobbie Maloy exposes the "Self-Betrayal Loop," a psychological trap where we constantly say yes to things that aren't us, effectively auditioning for everyone else's version of who we should be. Sharing her raw, personal journey through divorce, sudden identity shifts, and "identity moratorium," Bobbie challenges the modern self-help industry’s obsession with finding ourselves through addition. Instead, she reveals a simple, unconventional 10-minute exercise to help you draw a final line in the sand, proving that we don’t discover who we are by figuring out who we are supposed to be, but by courageously confronting who we are not. Bobbie Maloy is an author, business owner, U.S. Marine Corps veteran, and creator of The Aligned Self Method. After spending years navigating drastic identity shifts—from mi
title: How the Self-Betrayal Loop Traps You | Bobbie Maloy | TEDxThird Ward Salon

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if being a good patient doesn't mean being a quiet one? 

After years of medical dismissal before receiving a diagnosis of Stage IV endometriosis, licensed marriage and family therapist Aaliyah Maura realized that patient self-advocacy isn't about distrusting medical professionals- it's about becoming an informed, collaborative partner in your own healthcare decisions. In this powerful and deeply personal TEDx Talk, Aaliyah shares how learning to ask questions, recognize red and green flags in healthcare providers, and remain equally invested in her medical decisions ultimately changed the course of her life. 

Through compelling storytelling and practical insight, she challenges the belief that patients should blindly trust authority, encourages patients to re-evaluate the patient-doctor relationship, offering a compelling perspective on why advocating for yourself may be the most important decision a patient can make. While inspired by her personal health journey, Aaliyah's mes
title: Why you need to advocate for yourself at the doctor's office | Aaliyah Maura | TEDxThird Ward Salon

author: TEDx Talks
description: In 'Bekar Ko Akar', Neelam Sarangi shares her inspiring journey of transforming discarded, 'bekar' waste into meaningful and beautiful 'aakar'. She reveals how creativity and conscious thinking can turn the useless into useful, proving that sustainability begins with seeing value where others see waste. Neelam Sarangi is an Indian eco-entrepreneur and the founder of Bekar Ko Aakar, a social startup based in Jhansi, Uttar Pradesh, that focuses on upcycling solid waste into beautiful art pieces and functional products. Fondly nicknamed "Kabaad waali Didi" (The Scrap Sister), she has gained nationwide recognition for her work in transforming garbage into wealth. The literal meaning of her startup's name, Bekar Ko Aakar, is "Giving shape to the useless." She began her journey by collecting discarded materials like old tires, plastic bottles, metal scraps, copper wires, wooden logs, and shoes to creatively upcycle them into home decor, ornaments, and public art installations. This talk was
title: Bekar Ko Akar | Neelam Sarangi | TEDxBistupur

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Bir gün size en iyi olduğunuz şeyi bırakmanızı söyleseler kim olurdunuz?

Birkan Batuk, basketbol sahalarından başlayan ve bugünkü yolculuğuna uzanan hikâyesinden yola çıkarak dönüşümün hayatımızdaki yerini anlatıyor. Birkan Batuk, 18 yıl boyunca Türk ve Avrupa basketbolunun en üst seviyelerinde mücadele etmiş eski profesyonel basketbolcudur.

Türkiye Millî Takımı formasını 162 kez giyen Batuk, Anadolu Efes ile altı EuroLeague sezonunda mücadele etti. 2015 ve 2018 yıllarında Türkiye Kupası şampiyonluğu yaşarken, 2015 yılında Cumhurbaşkanlığı Kupası Finali’nin MVP’si seçildi. Ayrıca EuroCup finalinde mücadele etti; kariyeri boyunca Darüşşafaka, Pınar Karşıyaka ve Beşiktaş gibi önemli kulüplerde forma giydi.
